crosswalk.precise_difference: Stark uses seven transactional contract concepts; Adams uses language-function categories and treats conditions as expressed through those categories. The terms do not map one-to-one.
crosswalk.practical_consequence: Store both classifications and preserve each author’s terminology. Use them to inspect different aspects of a provision.
crosswalk.proposed_library_rule: Classify the bargain first, then describe how the wording performs that function; do not normalize the taxonomies into synonyms.
conditions_for_using_that_rule: A source-guided draft or review uses both books.

crosswalk.precise_difference: Stark emphasizes the deal concept and the relationship between a condition and an obligation; Adams emphasizes how wording and structure signal a condition and the risks of relying on a verb alone.
crosswalk.practical_consequence: Identify the business allocation, then test whether the text clearly signals it and states the linked duty.
crosswalk.proposed_library_rule: Record trigger, duty, actor, consequence, and any choice over who bears nonoccurrence risk.
conditions_for_using_that_rule: The clause conditions a duty, right, payment, or other legal relation.
legal_verification_needed: Applicable law governing conditions and remedies.

crosswalk.precise_difference: Stark treats representations and warranties as distinct remedy-related concepts. Adams specifically critiques treating represents/warrants labels as reliable remedy selectors and recommends plain fact-statement wording with remedies stated directly when needed.
crosswalk.practical_consequence: A house-style choice may affect negotiation and perceived risk; silently applying either terminology may hide a legal or commercial choice.
crosswalk.proposed_library_rule: Preserve both source positions, separate the factual statement from the negotiated remedy, and identify the applicable-law question.
conditions_for_using_that_rule: A provision makes a factual assertion or negotiates remedies for an inaccurate assertion.
legal_verification_needed: Current law governing the intended causes of action and remedies in the governing jurisdiction.

crosswalk.precise_difference: Stark emphasizes strategic scope and definitions as standards; Adams emphasizes reader-facing consistency, circularity, overlap, and efficient use.
crosswalk.practical_consequence: Definition review must cover both business scope and language behavior at every use.
crosswalk.proposed_library_rule: Treat a definition as a substantive rule when it changes scope, rights, duties, or standards; test every use and cross-reference.
conditions_for_using_that_rule: The contract defines or capitalizes a term.

crosswalk.precise_difference: Stark focuses on transaction parts and organizing business terms; Adams focuses on section layout, sequence, list presentation, and navigation.
crosswalk.practical_consequence: Use transaction logic to group provisions and a consistent layout to make them findable.
crosswalk.proposed_library_rule: Group related obligations and dependencies; use a stable section/list format; verify all schedules and exhibits against the body.
conditions_for_using_that_rule: Preparing or materially reorganizing an agreement.
legal_verification_needed: Verify incorporation and execution questions if they affect legal effect.

crosswalk.precise_difference: Stark discusses using the definition or interpretive section to address attachment status; Adams generally advises that a specific body reference is sufficient and a blanket “part of this agreement” sentence is unnecessary, with a stated master-agreement exception.
crosswalk.practical_consequence: The drafting choice affects whether the agreement includes global incorporation wording and how unmentioned or self-contained schedules are treated.
crosswalk.proposed_library_rule: Check each exact reference and the agreement structure; preserve the two recommendations and resolve the specific legal effect under governing law.
conditions_for_using_that_rule: A schedule, exhibit, form, or incorporated document affects performance, rights, or payment.
legal_verification_needed: Governing-law rules on incorporation and the exact contract text.

crosswalk.precise_difference: Stark offers a transaction-focused provision and whole-contract review workflow; Adams offers detailed language-level analysis of uncertainty and usage.
crosswalk.practical_consequence: Run the deal and cross-clause review first, then apply language-level checks to high-priority provisions.
crosswalk.proposed_library_rule: Do not rewrite the whole contract to house style; prioritize material business, operational, legal-verification, and ambiguity issues.
conditions_for_using_that_rule: Reviewing a contract received from another party.
legal_verification_needed: Issue-specific law and qualified professional review.

crosswalk.precise_difference: Not compared in this source-reading checkpoint. The books’ contents identify potentially relevant sections, but no claim of agreement or disagreement is made.
crosswalk.practical_consequence: Preserve each exception and do not state a source-based convention until relevant passages are reviewed.
